Part I / Foundations

Canonical decisions — the single source of truth for every contested definition

This section resolves all 15 concept drifts identified in the gap analysis. Every statement marked CANONICAL supersedes any prior version in any prior document. Every statement marked FIXED resolves an identified gap.

§01 The Three-Hub Architecture — replaces "dual-hub" (D06)

Canonical · D06 resolved

Journey OS uses a THREE-HUB ontology. The "dual-hub" framing (SubConcept + LearningObjective) from January 2026 design documents is deprecated. The three hubs are: SubConcept (what exists in medicine — knowledge hub), SLO (what the curriculum commits to teaching — pedagogical hub), USMLE_Subtopic (what the examination will test — assessment hub). Every AssessmentItem connects all three. The distinction matters for coverage reporting: COVERS_TOPIC (Session→SyllabusTopic) declares intent; TEACHES (ContentChunk→SubConcept) delivers evidence; CoverageRecord confirms verification.

THE THREE-HUB TOPOLOGY SLO ──CONTRIBUTES_TO──▸ ILO ← pedagogical hub: what curriculum commits to Session ──COVERS_TOPIC──▸ SyllabusTopic SyllabusTopic ──GROUNDED_IN──▸ StandardTerm ← LOD verification of declared topic ContentChunk ──TEACHES──▸ SubConcept ← knowledge hub: what lecture actually delivers SubConcept ──GROUNDED_IN──▸ StandardTerm ← LOD verification of extracted concept SubConcept ──HAS_COVERAGE──▸ CoverageRecord ← confirmed: taught + assessed SubConcept ──ALIGNS_TO──▸ USMLE_Subtopic ← assessment hub: what exam will test USMLE_Subtopic ──BELONGS_TO──▸ USMLE_Topic ──PART_OF──▸ USMLE_System AssessmentItem ──SOURCED_FROM──▸ ContentChunk AssessmentItem ──CLAIMS_ABOUT──▸ ProficiencyVariable SyllabusTopic = DECLARED intent (exists before any lecture uploaded) SubConcept = VERIFIED content (exists only after lecture ingested and LOD-confirmed) CoverageRecord = CONFIRMED coverage (TEACHES evidence ≥0.65 + ≥1 approved item → score starts)

§02 Canonical Definitions Register

Term / EdgeCanonical definitionResolves
GROUNDED_INPoints FROM a curriculum entity TO an external LOD entity. Meaning: "this curriculum concept has been verified against this standard term." Always: SubConcept → StandardTerm or SyllabusTopic → StandardTerm. The StandardTerm IS the LOD anchor; it never has a GROUNDED_IN edge of its own. GROUNDED_IN = LOD links only. Item provenance uses SOURCED_FROM.D03
TEACHES vs. COVERS_TOPICCOVERS_TOPIC (Session → SyllabusTopic) = declared curriculum intent from the syllabus document. Unverified. TEACHES (ContentChunk → SubConcept) = lecture-verified content delivery. LOD-confirmed. For LCME compliance evidence, only TEACHES chains count as verified coverage. The heatmap shows all three states: declared-only, delivered (no items yet), confirmed (CoverageRecord present).D07
CoverageRecordProgressive tracker, not binary. Created after the FIRST approved AssessmentItem SOURCED_FROM a ContentChunk TEACHING the SubConcept. coverage_score = approved_item_count / 3.0 (capped at 1.0). "Full coverage" = coverage_score = 1.0 = ≥3 approved items. Not created from COVERS_TOPIC chain alone — requires TEACHES evidence + assessment evidence both present.D02
SyllabusTopic vs. SubConceptSyllabusTopic: faculty-authored topic name from the syllabus document. Human authority. Can exist before any lecture is uploaded. Enriched with GROUNDED_IN → StandardTerm after NED. SubConcept: AI-extracted atomic teachable concept from lecture content. Machine-extracted, LOD-verified. Promoted from :Candidate label after faculty approval in P1 Step 07. Cannot exist without a source ContentChunk.D01
SLO CONTRIBUTES_TO ILODirection: SLO (child) → CONTRIBUTES_TO → ILO (parent). Read: "session learning objectives flow upward to institutional learning outcomes." Cypher: MATCH (slo:SLO)-[:CONTRIBUTES_TO]->(ilo:ILO). Never: MATCH (ilo)-[:CONTRIBUTES_TO]->(slo) — this is wrong direction. Audit: run MATCH (ilo:ILO)-[r:CONTRIBUTES_TO]->(slo:SLO) RETURN count(r) — must return 0.D09
LOD scope in generationThe lod_brief (Source 3) is ALWAYS included in generation context regardless of source_scope setting. The source_scope enum ('syllabus_only'|'lecture_only'|'usmle_only'|'combination') controls LOCAL chunks and STRUCTURED traversal. LOD is a pre-computed invariant that is always appended within the token budget. There is no configuration that excludes the LOD brief.D10
ContentChunk sizeCanonical: 150–250 tokens, 30-token overlap, entity-boundary-aligned. All prior references to "200-400 tokens, 50-token overlap" are deprecated. The reduction is required for: entity boundary preservation, BM25 performance, and retrieval precision.D04
Core generation modelCanonical: Claude Sonnet 4 (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) for core item generation and critique gate. Claude Haiku 4.5 for distractors, rationale, QA scoring, HyDE pre-call, and LOD brief. Any reference to "Opus for stem generation" in prior documents is deprecated. Cost basis: Sonnet core ≈ $0.027/item; full pipeline ≈ $0.12/item total. Opus would be $0.45/item — 3.75× budget overrun.D05
Event infrastructureCanonical for MSM MVP: Inngest only. 14 events defined with slash notation (journey/lecture.uploaded). Kafka is removed from the MVP. Inngest handles all workflow events at MSM scale. Kafka is a T5+ concern when scale exceeds Inngest per-event overhead (>1,000 simultaneous students). All Kafka topic references in prior documents are deprecated for the MVP.G13
EntityResolutionJob scopeNot orphaned by P1 redesign. P1 Step 05 handles automatic SAME_AS creation for CUI matches with confidence ≥ 0.85. EntityResolutionJob (Phase 5) handles: (1) SubConcepts with P1 confidence 0.65–0.84 — human review queue for ambiguous matches. (2) Cross-course deduplication where two SubConcepts from different courses evolved separately and now warrant comparison. (3) Periodic :Deprecated SubConcept cleanup. Batch-mode, not real-time.D08
8-Layer systemCanonical: 8-layer system numbered 0–7. Layer 0 = :Reference scaffold. Layers 1-2 = Institutional. Layer 3 = Content. Layer 4 = Taxonomy/Frameworks. Layer 5 = Assessment. Layer 6 = Exam. Layer 7 = Student. The 4-layer framing from January 2026 is deprecated. Any reference to "Layer 3" means the Content layer (SyllabusDocument, Lecture, ContentChunk, SubConcept nodes).D11
HyDE and ECDHyDE (Gao et al., 2022) is a retrieval engineering technique. It can be understood through an ECD lens — the hypothetical vignette operationalizes a related principle to ECD's exemplar performance. HyDE is NOT an ECD principle; it is a retrieval optimization that shares a related concept with ECD Stage 4 (Instance Specification). Do not assert equivalence between the two frameworks.G10
lod_brief storagelod_brief TEXT is stored in Supabase table subconcept_lod_briefs {subconcept_uuid FK, lod_brief TEXT, generated_at TIMESTAMP}. SubConcept node in Neo4j carries only lod_brief_id UUID (8 bytes — within skinny nodes <100 bytes limit). At generation time: fetch via Supabase single-key lookup (<5ms). Any prior code referencing sc.lod_brief as a Neo4j property is deprecated. Update all code examples.G05, D12

§03 Evidence Grade Weights — enabling path confidence computation (G06)

Fixed · G06 resolved — evidence_grade now computable

Evidence grade is a string enum on all edges. Path confidence requires numeric multiplication. The following mapping is canonical for all WisdomPath computations.

// constants/graph-schema.ts — add to all projects
export const EVIDENCE_GRADE_WEIGHT: Record<EvidenceGrade, number> = {
  A: 1.00,  // Seeded taxonomy or faculty-verified (ground truth)
  B: 0.82,  // GNN-predicted (HeteroSAGE link prediction, high confidence)
  C: 0.65,  // System-inferred before faculty review (P1 initial TEACHES edges)
  D: 0.45,  // Sparse signal (LOD-only, no curriculum corroboration)
};

// Path confidence: product of edge weights along chain
// Example: ContentChunk -[C]→ SubConcept -[A]→ StandardTerm -[B]→ ExternalEntity
// path_confidence = 0.65 × 1.00 × 0.82 = 0.533
const pathConfidence = (grades: EvidenceGrade[]): number =>
  grades.reduce((acc, g) => acc * EVIDENCE_GRADE_WEIGHT[g], 1.0);

// All edges must also carry evidence_weight: Float computed from this map at creation time
// Enables direct Cypher multiplication without application-layer mapping

§04 Dual-Write with Reconciliation (G08)

Fixed · G08 resolved

Supabase writes first. Neo4j writes second. Never block on Neo4j failure. But silent inconsistency is unacceptable — every Supabase row that has a Neo4j counterpart carries sync status.

-- Migration: add to all tables with Neo4j counterparts
ALTER TABLE subconcepts
  ADD COLUMN neo4j_synced_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN neo4j_sync_status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'
  CHECK (neo4j_sync_status IN ('pending', 'synced', 'failed'));

// Weekly reconciliation Inngest job: journey/sync.reconcile (Monday 1am)
const reconcile = async () => {
  // Find rows that failed or never synced
  const unsynced = await supabase
    .from('subconcepts')
    .select('uuid, name, cui')
    .or('neo4j_sync_status.eq.pending,neo4j_sync_status.eq.failed');
  // Re-attempt Neo4j MERGE (deterministic UUIDs — always idempotent)
  for (const row of unsynced.data) {
    try {
      await neo4j.run(`MERGE (sc:SubConcept:Candidate {uuid:$uuid}) SET sc.name=$name`, row);
      await supabase.from('subconcepts').update({ neo4j_synced_at: new Date(), neo4j_sync_status: 'synced' }).eq('uuid', row.uuid);
    } catch { await supabase.from('subconcepts').update({ neo4j_sync_status: 'failed' }).eq('uuid', row.uuid); }
  }
};

§12 Five-shot examples for text2Cypher (G03)

const FEW_SHOT_EXAMPLES = [
  {
    query_hash: sha256('usmle systems fewest items'),
    natural_language: 'Which USMLE systems have the fewest approved assessment items?',
    cypher: `
      MATCH (sys:USMLE_System)
      OPTIONAL MATCH (sys)<-[:PART_OF]-(:USMLE_Topic)<-[:BELONGS_TO]-(:USMLE_Subtopic)
                      <-[:ALIGNS_TO]-(sc:SubConcept)<-[:SOURCED_FROM]-(i:AssessmentItem {status:'approved'})
      RETURN sys.name AS system, count(i) AS approved_items
      ORDER BY approved_items ASC LIMIT 5`
  },
  {
    query_hash: sha256('student mastery below threshold renal'),
    natural_language: 'Which students have mastery below 50% in Renal?',
    cypher: `
      MATCH (s:Student)-[:HAS_MASTERY]->(sm:StudentMastery)-[:FOR_CONCEPT]->(sc:SubConcept)
             -[:ALIGNS_TO]->(sub:USMLE_Subtopic)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(t:USMLE_Topic)
             -[:PART_OF]->(sys:USMLE_System {name:'Renal'})
      WHERE sm.p_mastery < 0.5
      RETURN s.uuid, sc.name, sm.p_mastery
      ORDER BY sm.p_mastery ASC`
  },
  {
    query_hash: sha256('drugs treat diseases GI curriculum'),
    natural_language: 'What drugs taught in the GI curriculum treat diseases associated with those concepts?',
    cypher: `
      MATCH (ch:ContentChunk)-[t:TEACHES]->(sc:SubConcept)-[:GROUNDED_IN]->(st:StandardTerm)
      MATCH (sc)-[:ALIGNS_TO]->(sub:USMLE_Subtopic)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(top:USMLE_Topic)
             -[:PART_OF]->(sys:USMLE_System {name:'Gastrointestinal'})
      MATCH (drug:Compound)-[:TREATS]->(st)
      RETURN DISTINCT drug.name AS drug, sc.name AS concept LIMIT 20`
  },
  {
    query_hash: sha256('SLOs no approved assessment items'),
    natural_language: 'Which SLOs have no approved assessment items at all?',
    cypher: `
      MATCH (slo:SLO)-[:COVERS_TOPIC]->(st:SyllabusTopic)
      WHERE NOT (slo)<-[:ASSESSED_BY]-(:AssessmentItem {status:'approved'})
      RETURN slo.uuid, slo.text, st.name LIMIT 20`
  },
  {
    query_hash: sha256('cardiovascular coverage heatmap'),
    natural_language: 'Show the coverage heatmap for Cardiovascular: which SubConcepts have confirmed coverage and which are gaps?',
    cypher: `
      MATCH (sc:SubConcept)-[:ALIGNS_TO]->(sub:USMLE_Subtopic)-[:BELONGS_TO]->(top:USMLE_Topic)
             -[:PART_OF]->(sys:USMLE_System {name:'Cardiovascular'})
      OPTIONAL MATCH (sc)-[:HAS_COVERAGE]->(cr:CoverageRecord)
      RETURN sc.name, top.name AS topic,
             CASE WHEN cr IS NULL THEN 'gap' WHEN cr.coverage_score < 1.0 THEN 'partial' ELSE 'confirmed' END AS status,
             coalesce(cr.coverage_score, 0) AS score
      ORDER BY score ASC`
  },
];

Part IV / Three Pipelines

All gaps applied: LCMEDomainClassifier · lod_brief→Supabase · ECD stages · Sonnet canonical

§13 Pipeline 1 — Ingestion (journey/lecture.process)

Latency-sensitive. Faculty-visible. <5 min target for 50-slide lecture. Priority: high. Timeout: 15min. Retries: 3. Concurrency: 10 per faculty_id.

01
parse PPTX / PDF
Structural parsing. PPTX: one LectureSection per slide = title + body_text. Speaker notes → separate SpeakerNote nodes (faculty intent, not student-facing). PDF: layout-aware heading detection. Emits status: 'parsing' to Supabase.
02
create-graph-scaffold MERGE + deterministicUUID
Lecture + LectureSection nodes + HAS_SECTION edges. ALL writes use MERGE with deterministic UUIDs — re-uploading never creates duplicates. Sets neo4j_sync_status: 'synced' on Supabase row.
03
graph-aware-chunk D04: 150-250 tokens
Entity-boundary-aligned chunking. Target: 150–250 tokens, 30-token overlap (canonical). Heading context prepended for embedding. USMLE_System context from course used as domain hint for entity recognition within chunker. Max 3 chunks per LectureSection.
04
multi-embed 3 granularities · domain-aware
Parallel embedding: (1) Chunk embeddings — MedCPT if entity_density >0.3, else text-embedding-3-small. (2) Section embeddings — full slide text. (3) Lecture summary — Claude Haiku ~150 tokens then embedded. Stored in Supabase pgvector.
05
extract-entities Batched UMLS · 20/call
Medical NER across all chunks. UMLS batch lookup (20 entities per call — not sequential). LLM disambiguation if confidence <0.80. SAME_AS detection: if CUI matches existing SubConcept AND confidence ≥0.85 → create SAME_AS immediately. If confidence 0.65–0.84 → defer to EntityResolutionJob queue.
05b
lcme-domain-classify NEW · G04 resolved
Claude Haiku classifies each ContentChunk against the 20 LCMEContentDomain node descriptions (Standard 7.1–7.9). Confidence ≥0.70 → create COVERS_LCME_DOMAIN edge with {confidence, method: 'classifier'}. This step was completely absent from prior pipeline specs — without it, the LCME Standard 7 compliance map stays empty permanently.
06
create-teaches-edges Hybrid RRF · evidence_grade: 'C'
BM25 + dense RRF (k=60) for candidate SubConcept matching. TEACHES edges created with evidence_grade: 'C' and evidence_weight: 0.65. SubConcept nodes created as :Candidate. Sets embedding_source: 'text_only' (cold-start flag).
07
faculty-review-gate step.waitForEvent · 7-day window
Inngest function SUSPENDS. No polling. Awaits journey/lecture.reviewed event. Timeout: 7 days. On timeout: auto-approve confidence ≥0.85, flag rest as 'review_overdue'.
08
finalize-graph Fan-out · one event per approved SubConcept
Approved: remove :Candidate label, upgrade evidence_grade: 'C' → 'A' (evidence_weight: 1.0). Fan-out: step.sendEvent() fires journey/subconcept.confirmed for each approved SubConcept. These trigger P2 independently. Update neo4j_synced_at on Supabase rows.

§14 Pipeline 2 — Enrichment (journey/subconcept.enrich)

Background. Rate-limit-aware. Timeout: 24hr. Retries: 5. Concurrency: 5. Faculty never sees this pipeline directly.

01
umls-resolve
Full UMLS Metathesaurus lookup: preferred term, semantic type, all cross-references (SNOMED, MeSH, ICD-10, RxNorm). LLM disambiguation using all TEACHES chunk text + USMLE_System context. Creates/merges StandardTerm. Creates GROUNDED_IN edge.
02
anatomy-disease-link semantic_type routing
Routes by semantic_type_label (T022→AnatomicalSystem, T023→AnatomicalOrgan, T024/T025/T026→AnatomicalStructure, T029→AnatomicalRegion, T047→DiseaseCategory, T121→Compound). Creates: AFFECTS_ORGAN, HAS_FINDING_SITE, CLASSIFIED_IN, MEDIATED_BY, PRESENTS_AS, TREATS edges.
03
hetionet-import CUI merge · 2-hop selective
CUI match to Hetionet. Import 2-hop neighborhood. Allowed edge types: Drug-treats-Disease, Disease-associates-Gene, Gene-participates-Pathway, Drug-binds-Gene, Disease-presents-Symptom. Max 10 nodes per type. Sets embedding_source: 'graph_augmented'.
04
lod-brief-generate → Supabase · G05 resolved
Generate ~200-token LOD brief (Claude Haiku). Store in Supabase subconcept_lod_briefs table. SubConcept node in Neo4j receives only lod_brief_id FK (8 bytes — within skinny nodes limit). At generation time: single Supabase key-value lookup (<5ms). Evidence of canonical fix: sc.lod_brief property REMOVED; sc.lod_brief_id FK ADDED.
05
cross-lecture-link
Find other lectures teaching this SubConcept. Create EXPLAINS_SAME_CONCEPT edges between ContentChunks from different lectures. Enables: "find all content about furosemide regardless of which lecture" as a single Cypher pattern.
06
proficiency-variable-create NEW · ECD Student Model
Create ProficiencyVariable node 1:1 with confirmed SubConcept. Properties: name (same as SubConcept.name), grain_size: 'subconcept', evidence_threshold: 0.85, mastery_definition (Claude Haiku generates from SubConcept description). Create MAPPED_TO edge: SubConcept → ProficiencyVariable. Create ASSESSED_BY edges: ProficiencyVariable → TaskShell (matched by concept_family).
07
gnn-retrain-check
If new confirmed SubConcepts since last retrain >100: emit journey/gnn.retrain-trigger. HeteroSAGE retrain on faculty-approved TEACHES edges (grade: 'A'). Post-retrain: new predicted TEACHES edges added with evidence_grade: 'B', evidence_weight: 0.82. Affected SubConcepts get embedding_source: 'full_gnn'.

§15 Pipeline 3 — Generation (journey/items.batch-generate)

On-demand. Canonical model: Sonnet for core + critique. Haiku for HyDE, distractors, rationale, QA. D05 Timeout: 30min per batch.

00
specification-conversation OUTSIDE Inngest · Chat UI
Faculty defines spec. System proposes gap-aware defaults: SubConcepts with no CoverageRecord listed first. Coverage-aware: excludes SubConcepts already meeting blueprint proportion. Max 10 turns. On confirmation → emit journey/generation.spec-confirmed.
ECD1
identify-proficiency-variable ECD Stage 1
For each target: MATCH (sc)-[:MAPPED_TO]->(pv:ProficiencyVariable). Returns: pv.grain_size, pv.evidence_threshold, pv.mastery_definition. This is "what KSA are we measuring?" — not just "what SubConcept are we targeting."
ECD2
define-evidence-rules ECD Stage 2 · Haiku
Claude Haiku generates evidence rules for a 5-option item: what mastery does the correct response demonstrate? What specific misconception does each distractor target? These become Distractor.evidence_rule properties. Grounds "Why Wrong?" explanations in a named misconception, not post-hoc inference.
ECD3
select-task-shell ECD Stage 3 · Graph query
MATCH (pv)-[:ASSESSED_BY]->(ts:TaskShell) WHERE ts.bloom_range contains spec.bloom_level AND ts.concept_family = target.concept_family ORDER BY ts.avg_quality_score DESC LIMIT 1. If no matching shell → HyDE step still runs; item is generated free-form but flagged for TaskShell library expansion.
01
hyde-context-assembly HyDE · Parallel 4-source · lod_brief from Supabase
HyDE: Claude Haiku generates 2-sentence hypothetical vignette (100 tokens) → embed → RRF k=60. Then parallel fan-out: LOCAL (HyDE-embedded hybrid RRF + Parent Doc Retriever hop), STRUCTURED (USMLE alignment), LOD (Supabase subconcept_lod_briefs lookup — <5ms), GLOBAL (ConceptCluster summary if available — T4+). Token budget: LOCAL 3,000 / STRUCTURED 800 / LOD 500 / GLOBAL 400.
02
generate-core D05: Claude Sonnet 4
Clinical vignette + correct answer only. No distractors. Structured output: {stem, patient_age, patient_sex, clinical_setting, lead_in_type, correct_answer, answer_mechanism, source_chunk_uuids[]}. TaskShell.variable_slots provides the template structure.
03
critique-gate Sonnet-as-critic · max 2 retries
Sonnet reviews for clinical coherence + educational validity + NBME format. Failed items: regenerate with critique as additional context. Items passing critique proceed. ECD alignment check also here: does the item actually claim what pv.mastery_definition states?
04
generate-distractors Haiku · MisconceptionCategory-grounded
4 distractors, each anchored to a MisconceptionCategory node queried from graph (ordered by empirical_frequency DESC). Each distractor gets: text, is_correct: false, evidence_rule (from ECD Stage 2), TARGETS_MISCONCEPTION edge to the relevant MisconceptionCategory node.
05
generate-rationale + QA Haiku
Rationale with source citations (ContentChunk UUIDs). QA: 22-rule NBME validation + medical_accuracy + coherence + blueprint_fit. Toulmin chain generated and stored in Supabase assessment_items.toulmin (JSONB — never traversed in graph). Items below QA threshold flagged, not auto-rejected.
06
provenance-write → faculty-approval → post-approval step.waitForEvent · 30-day
AssessmentItem + Distractor + Rationale written. All 9 typed classification edges created. INSTANTIATES → TaskShell. CLAIMS_ABOUT → ProficiencyVariable. Then: suspend until journey/items.batch-reviewed. On approval: update CoverageRecord (coverage_score = count/3 capped 1.0), init BKT_Parameters, add to practice pool.

§17 StudyQueue recommendation algorithm (G14)

Fixed · G14 — spaced repetition algorithm specified

BKT decay identifies declining mastery. The recommendation algorithm (not previously defined) specifies which item to recommend and when.

// StudyQueue recommendation — Inngest function: journey/studyqueue.generate
// Triggered: student opens Practice, or daily at 8am per student (cron)

async function generateStudyQueue(studentUuid: string): Promise<PracticeCollection> {
  // Step 1: Identify concepts due for review (BKT decay + time since last attempt)
  const dueConcepts = await neo4j.run(`
    MATCH (s:Student {uuid:$uuid})-[:HAS_MASTERY]->(sm:StudentMastery)-[:FOR_CONCEPT]->(sc:SubConcept)
    WHERE sm.p_mastery < 0.75                              // below mastery threshold
      OR duration.inDays(sm.last_updated, datetime()).days >  // overdue per decay halflife
         CASE sc.domain
           WHEN 'Anatomy' THEN 120
           WHEN 'Pharmacology' THEN 60
           WHEN 'Clinical Skills' THEN 180
           ELSE 90
         END * 0.5                                        // practice at half the halflife
    OPTIONAL MATCH (sc)-[:HAS_COVERAGE]->(cr:CoverageRecord)
    RETURN sc.uuid, sc.clinical_consequence_score,
           sm.p_mastery, sm.last_updated,
           cr.coverage_score AS coverage
    ORDER BY sc.clinical_consequence_score * (1 - sm.p_mastery) DESC LIMIT 10
  `, { uuid: studentUuid });

  // Step 2: Select item using IRT information maximization
  // Pick item with highest information at student's estimated theta
  const theta = await estimateStudentAbility(studentUuid); // from BKT p_mastery → IRT theta
  const items = await selectItemsByIRTInformation(dueConcepts, theta, { maxSeen: false });

  // Step 3: Create RecommendationEvent nodes for audit trail
  for (const item of items) {
    await neo4j.run(`
      MERGE (re:RecommendationEvent {uuid: $uuid})
        ON CREATE SET re.algorithm = 'spaced_retrieval_v1',
          re.trigger_reason = 'bkt_decay_below_threshold',
          re.scheduled_for = datetime(), re.item_uuid = $item
    `, { uuid: det(`rec:${studentUuid}:${item.uuid}:${Date.now()}`), item: item.uuid });
  }
  return { items, algorithm: 'spaced_retrieval_v1' };
}

Part VI / ECD Framework

Evidence-Centered Design — the reason the assessment is valid

Core principle

Without ECD, Journey OS generates questions. With ECD, Journey OS generates defensible assessments. Every item carries a principled argument answering: "Why does this question constitute valid evidence of mastery of this competency at this cognitive level?"

Student Model
What KSAs are we measuring?

KG: SubConcept · ProficiencyVariable · BKT_Parameters · StudentMastery · IRT_Parameters. The SubConcept × USMLE × Bloom alignment graph IS the construct map. ProficiencyVariable formalizes grain size and mastery thresholds.

Task Model
What situations elicit evidence?

KG: TaskShell (12 seeded templates) · AssessmentItem with 9 typed classification edges. Each item INSTANTIATES a TaskShell. Task variables = Bloom level, lead-in type, clinical setting, patient demographics, variable slots.

Evidence Model
How does performance constitute evidence?

KG property: Distractor.evidence_rule (text). Supabase JSONB: assessment_items.toulmin. BKT update function IS the evidence accumulation function. IRT likelihood IS the evidence weight. Stored in Supabase — never traversed in graph.

ECD design decisions — what stays in Neo4j vs. Supabase

ComponentStorageRationale
TaskShellNeo4j nodeQueried: which templates produce best items? avg_quality_score ordering. Graph traversal: PV → ASSESSED_BY → TaskShell.
ProficiencyVariableNeo4j nodeTraversed: SubConcept → MAPPED_TO → PV → ASSESSED_BY → TaskShell. Core ECD path.
AssessmentArgument (Toulmin)Supabase JSONBDisplay artifact — faculty review panel only. Key-value lookup: "show me Toulmin for item X". Never traversed.
Distractor.evidence_ruleNeo4j property (not node)Item-specific. Never queried independently. Analytics use TARGETS_MISCONCEPTION → MisconceptionCategory (that IS traversable).

HyDE and ECD — the corrected framing (G10)

Canonical · G10 resolved

HyDE (Gao et al., 2022) is a retrieval engineering technique. It can be understood through an ECD lens — the hypothetical vignette operationalizes a related principle to ECD's Stage 4 exemplar performance. HyDE is NOT an ECD principle and claiming equivalence between the two frameworks is a category error that reviewers would flag. State as: "HyDE operationalizes a related ECD principle" — never "HyDE IS ECD."

Part VII / Product & Roadmap

Six personas · 18-month roadmap · All sequencing fixes applied

§22 The MVP loop — the one sentence that defines the product

Upload Monday · Exam Friday

Admin sets up institution → Faculty uploads syllabus + lectures → AI extracts concepts + enriches with UMLS/Hetionet → Faculty generates NBME-quality items (~$0.12 each, ~$3/30-item batch) → Faculty reviews, refines, approves via component-targeted editing → Faculty assembles blueprint-validated exam → Student takes exam → Student sees mastery map + "Why Wrong?" FERPA compliance — architectural guarantees

  • Row-Level Security on every Supabase table scoped to institution_id — PostgreSQL-enforced, not application-layer
  • Student data never crosses institutional boundaries — UUID bridge keys are institution-scoped
  • Audit log table: every read/write to student data logged with actor_id, action, timestamp, resource_uuid

Part X / Production Readiness — Canonical Decisions

45 findings resolved — the decisions that separate demo from deployment

Every finding in the production readiness analysis (C01–C10, H01–H13, M01–M10, architecture gaps) has been reviewed and resolved as canonical decisions below. These supersede any prior document where they conflict. A system meeting all decisions in this section is production-grade for an LCME-accredited medical school with real exams and real student grades.

§P1 Exam Integrity — the non-negotiables

Canonical — C01 resolved: Answer auto-save

Every student answer is persisted server-side on selection, not on final submission. The session_answers table is the mutable draft state; the attempts table is the immutable final record. On exam resume after crash, answers are restored from session_answers. Attempts are created atomically from session_answers on final submit. This is the difference between a testing system and a toy.

Canonical — C02 resolved: Time-windowed item access

Students access assessment item content ONLY during an active exam session. The RLS policy on assessment_items checks: student role may read an item ONLY IF an active session (started_at > now() - 4 hours AND completed_at IS NULL) exists for that student containing that item. Faculty and admin always have full read access. Pre-fetching items before an exam window is architecturally impossible.

Canonical — H05 resolved: Per-student item and option randomization

Every exam session generates a deterministic random order seeded by (student_id + exam_id) for items and (student_id + item_id) for options. These shuffle maps are stored in sessions.item_order_seed and sessions.option_shuffle_seed. The "correct answer" is never stored as a positional index — it is always the UUID of the correct option, resolved against the shuffle at display time. Exam records store the item version number used (not just item_id) for post-exam legal defensibility.

Canonical — Exam timing model

Exams have three timestamps: available_from (when students can start), available_until (hard close — submissions after this time are rejected), results_release_at (when students see scores and rationale — separate from submission close for summative exams). ADA accommodations are stored in student_accommodations (student_id, exam_id, time_multiplier, approved_by). The exam delivery service applies the multiplier to time_limit_mins per student.

§P2 Security & Multi-tenancy

Canonical — C05 resolved: Neo4j tenant isolation via wrapper, never raw driver

All Neo4j queries must go through neo4jQuery(cypher, params, ctx) — never through the raw driver. The wrapper: (1) injects institution_id parameter automatically from the request context, (2) validates that the Cypher string accepts $institution_id as a parameter (compile-time check), (3) returns a configurable fallback value instead of throwing on connection failure. Direct driver.executeQuery() calls are banned by ESLint rule. CI fails if any are detected.

Canonical — H12 resolved: Prompt injection prevention

All lecture content entering any LLM prompt is: (1) sanitized via sanitizeForContext() which redacts common injection patterns, and (2) wrapped in XML delimiters (<lecture_content>...</lecture_content>, <lod_brief>...</lod_brief>). Generation prompts begin "Using ONLY the information in <lecture_content>..." This creates an explicit boundary the model respects between instruction and data. Applied to ALL content entering P1, P2, and P3 prompts without exception.

Canonical — C10 resolved: Generation rate limits

Three layers: (1) API middleware enforces max 3 concurrent P3 runs per faculty_id. (2) Before triggering P3 for >10 items: cost estimate shown, confirmation required. (3) Daily limit: max 100 items generated per faculty per calendar day (configurable per institution via institution_generation_limits table). Tracked in generation_daily_usage (faculty_id, date, items_count). Institutions can request limit increases via admin dashboard.

Canonical — C06 resolved: Model version pinning

Model strings are pinned as exact versioned identifiers in environment variables (ANTHROPIC_MODEL_SONNET=claude-sonnet-4-20250514, ANTHROPIC_MODEL_HAIKU=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) and verified on application startup with a known test prompt. Every generated item records the exact generation_model string used. If Anthropic retires a model, the startup check catches it before any faculty session begins and disables generation until the env var is updated. Items generated in 2026 can be traced to the exact model version that produced them.

Canonical — C10 resolved: Three-layer generation rate control

(1) API concurrency: max 3 concurrent P3 runs per faculty_id enforced at Inngest config and API middleware. (2) Confirmation gate: generating >10 items requires faculty to confirm a displayed cost estimate before the batch triggers — prevents accidental 100-item submits. (3) Daily quota: max 100 items generated per faculty per calendar day, tracked in generation_daily_usage, configurable per institution via institution_generation_limits. Exceeding quota returns HTTP 429 with time-until-reset.

§P3 Data Integrity

Canonical — C03 resolved: Atomic CoverageRecord increments

CoverageRecord updates always use atomic Neo4j SET expressions — never read-modify-write. The Cypher expression SET cr.assessment_count = cr.assessment_count + 1 is atomic within a single Cypher statement. For concurrent approvals that need mutual exclusion, use Supabase advisory lock: SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('coverage:' || subconcept_uuid)) before the P3 post-approval Neo4j write.

Canonical — C08 resolved: P1 cleanup on failure

All P1 pipeline functions have an onFailure handler that: (1) marks the lecture status = 'failed', (2) emits journey/pipeline.failed triggering admin alert, (3) cleans up orphaned ContentChunks (those with no TEACHES edges from this lecture run), (4) removes :Candidate SubConcept nodes created by this run. A weekly integrity check queries for ContentChunks with no TEACHES edges and alerts admin if count > 50.

Canonical — C09 resolved: SAME_AS cycle prevention

Before creating any SAME_AS edge A→B, the pipeline checks whether B can already reach A via SAME_AS traversal (depth 1-5). If a cycle would be created, the edge is skipped and the ambiguity is logged to entity_resolution_conflicts for manual review. Direction convention: SAME_AS edges always point from lower CUI string → higher CUI string, making the direction deterministic and preventing bidirectional duplicates.

Canonical — C07 resolved: LOD brief versioning and expiry

subconcept_lod_briefs carries lod_brief_version INT and umls_release TEXT. A quarterly Inngest cron (0 9 1 */3 *) compares stored release against current UMLS release. Briefs for SubConcepts with clinical_consequence_score > 0.7 are regenerated first (highest patient-safety impact). Briefs older than 180 days trigger live UMLS fallback in context assembly instead of the stale brief. The lod_brief_history table preserves prior versions for audit.

§P4 Clinical Safety

Canonical — H11 resolved: Clinical confidence tier system

Every AssessmentItem carries clinical_confidence TEXT CHECK (clinical_confidence IN ('unverified','self_verified','peer_reviewed','expert_reviewed')). Generated items start as 'unverified'. Faculty approval → 'self_verified'. Items with usmle_subtopic.clinical_consequence_score > 0.85 require a second faculty reviewer before entering the exam pool → 'peer_reviewed'. Expert review (T4+ feature, by clinical education specialist) → 'expert_reviewed'. The exam assembly algorithm can be configured to require a minimum tier — summative exams should require at minimum 'self_verified'. Blueprint UI shows tier distribution. This is the framing difference LCME reviewers care about: "AI-assisted drafting reviewed by clinical experts" vs. "AI-generated content in high-stakes assessment."

§P5 Reliability

Canonical — C04 resolved: Dead letter queue and manual retry

All three pipelines have onFailure handlers that write to pipeline_dead_letters (pipeline, entity_id, inngest_run_id, error_message, step_name, failed_at, retried_at). Admin dashboard shows dead letter count with drill-down. Manual retry endpoint: POST /app/api/admin/pipelines/dead-letters/[id]/retry which re-emits the original trigger event. A Slack/email alert fires when any dead letter is created for a P3 pipeline (item generation failure) or when dead letter count exceeds 10 in 1 hour for P1/P2.

Canonical — H06 resolved: JSON repair and per-item failure isolation

All Claude API responses are parsed via safeJsonParse() which attempts: (1) direct JSON.parse, (2) jsonrepair() then parse, (3) returns null. All P3 batch operations use Promise.allSettled() not Promise.all() — one malformed response does not fail the batch. Items that fail JSON parsing: status set to 'generation_failed', logged to pipeline_runs step_log, excluded from the batch result. The batch continues with remaining items. A batch with >20% failure rate emits an admin alert.

Canonical — Keep-warm cron for sidecars

A journey/cron.keep-warm Inngest function runs every 10 minutes during business hours (7am-10pm institution timezone) sending a trivial embed request to MedCPT and a trivial render request to the pptx-renderer sidecar. This prevents Railway/Fly.io cold starts during active faculty hours. The cron is disabled outside business hours to reduce cost. Cost: ~$0.50/month in Haiku calls.

Two new Neo4j node types from production analysis: FacultyWarning (extracted from speaker notes — "WARNS_AGAINST" edges to explicit misconception warnings, reviewed quarterly to update MisconceptionCategory seed) and ItemFlag (tracks clinical review requests with reviewer assignment and resolution status). The total node type count remains manageable at 79. All other new entities live in Supabase (session_answers, item_versions, etc.) per the Supabase-first invariant — they are operational/transactional data, not graph-structure data.
